summary: Scheduled credit reallocation caused by legacy rate-tag cascade leading to mid-cycle invoice variance
description: Issue summary: Customer reports an unexpected mid-cycle adjustment where scheduled reserve credits were reallocated between projects, producing a negative provisional line on the most recent invoice. Impact: ClarifyAI observed ~9.7% higher billed usage on their March 1-12 provisional invoice; autopay is blocked by a negative provisional line. Environment: prod-us-east, enterprise account with dedicated reserved blocks and hosted fallback. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run daily batch-embed job using key proj-clarify-prod (batch window 03:00 UTC). 2) Observe hourly postbacks for March 10–12 and compare to console estimate. 3) Check billing ledger and reserve credit assignment for subprojects. Expected behavior: scheduled reserve credits should remain pinned to the original subproject and not be reallocated mid-cycle unless an explicit renewal/plan change is applied. Actual behavior: on 2026-03-11 at 02:12 UTC an automated reallocation ran that moved several hourly buffer credits from the subproject "clarify-embed" to "clarify-core"; associated provisional line shows a negative adjustment and blocked autopay. Logs/attachments: customer supplied invoice PDF (attached), sample postback payloads (attached), and a screenshot of Console Billing -> Usage timeline. Customer request: immediate reconciliation and provisional credit reversal so autopay can proceed; explain root cause and preventive action.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 08:10 — pulled ledger rows: invoice_id inv-2026-03-prov-clarify; negative item -10,243.00 tokens-equivalent. Postback sequence shows ordering gap 02:11:50–02:12:50 with mixed tags (legacy_rate_tag: rate-A (deprecated) and active_rate_tag: rate-B).

Reconciler dry-run: repro when legacy-to-active tag migration happens during the hourly allocator sweep — algorithm currently treats unmapped/unknown tags as eligible for automatic reallocation to 'default' cost-center. The cleanup PR removed mappings causing temporarily unknown tag state for ~3 minutes.

Hypothesis: cleanup PR (#4112) removed a mapping that the hourly allocator relied on; when the allocator encountered an unmapped tag it triggered a catch-all reallocation routine that moved buffer credits across subprojects. This happened only on hosts processing mixed-queue microbatches (embed + chat) which matches ClarifyAI's mixed workload pattern.
Query results: Number of affected reallocations = 7 (hours) across 2026-03-11 02:00–05:00 UTC. Total credits moved: 27 buffer-hours. Estimated cost delta: ~9.7% on provisional invoice.
resolution: Workaround applied: Billing team applied a provisional reversal ledger entry on 2026-03-14 12:45 UTC to restore credits to original subproject and cleared autopay block — confirmed with customer. Permanent fix: reverted cleanup PR mapping removal and added a safe-guard in allocator to treat unmapped rate-tags as 'no-op' (PR 4128). Rollout notes: fix deployed to reconciler staging 2026-03-14 09:00 UTC and to prod 2026-03-14 11:30 UTC with a 2-hour monitoring window. Follow-ups: (1) schedule a postmortem with reconciler and billing teams (owner: Marco Alvarez) due 2026-03-18, (2) add unit tests for tag-migration safety, (3) notify customers with similar mixed-queue patterns via billing bulletin. Customer confirmation: ClarifyAI acknowledged provisional reversal and requested final invoice adjustment once monthly close completes.
